exercise_name: Audience empathy / Move From → Move To map
description: Participant analyzes their target audience and maps where the audience is now versus where they want them to end up (Move From/Move To), defining the audience transformation before building any content.
Participant distills their entire presentation into a single clear, persuasive 'Big Idea' sentence that states a point of view and what is at stake, used as the spine of the talk.

exercise_name: Sparkline mapping (what is / what could be)
description: Participant structures their talk by alternating between 'what is' and 'what could be' to build contrast and momentum toward a call to action, plotting the talk on Duarte's Sparkline narrative arc.

Participant writes each main point on a physical sticky note, then arranges and rearranges them on a table or wall to find a compelling flow before building slides — an analog ideation drill done with worksheets and marker pens.
Participant hand-sketches visual concepts for slides and builds a manual storyboard, taping printed slides alongside sticky notes to develop visual thinking without software.

Participant designs a 'Something They'll Always Remember' — a memorable dramatized moment (repeatable sound bite, evocative visual, emotive story, shocking stat, or staged demo) to anchor the audience's recall.
In the DataStory workshop participant uses story structure to turn a data set into a clear executive summary and recommendation, practicing how to frame numbers as a narrative.

description: Learner watches/works through a demonstrated mock negotiation (e.g., negotiating a salary increase) applying tactical empathy and mirroring; community members run optional live negotiation practice sessions to roleplay with peers.

On day 1 learner completes a self-assessment benchmarking their speaking and communication skills, then repeats it at the end of the 31-day quest as a before/after measure.
Learner practices the 'verbal highlighting' technique — slowing the pace, lowering the voice, and adding assertive 'voice spikes' to emphasize key words and phrases when speaking.
Learner practices using a deliberate breathing pause as a strategic tool to emphasize key points and create anticipation.

exercise_name: Valley Technique (sharing a low point + lesson)
description: Learner practices an emotional storytelling structure: celebrate an accomplishment, then share an all-time low point in their life, then share the lesson learned — to speak authentically and vulnerably.
Learner practices 'care-frontation' — a compassionate, empathetic way to address difficult or confrontational conversations.

exercise_name: Shaping a Story / painting a vivid image
description: Learner practices structuring and delivering a story that paints a vivid mental image and conveys emotion, as a recurring craft drill across the quest.

Toward the end of the quest the learner is encouraged to host an event and deliver a real speech applying the techniques learned — a field assignment in front of a live audience.

provider: Coursera — Introduction to Public Speaking (Univ. of Washington, Matt McGarrity)

Learner strikes up low-stakes conversations (e.g., with coworkers) and practices keeping flow by noticing and following up on 'free information'/hooks the other person offers.
Learner selects a single social skill to master and practices it deliberately every day, building it the way one would drill a foreign language.
Learner practices telling a short conversational story that holds interest, builds connection, and lands a satisfying conclusion using vivid value-adding details — a chapter with worked guidance.
Step-by-step guidance/exercises for meeting new people, deepening acquaintances into friendships, and supporting friends — applied through real-world social outings.
Learner applies the dating chapter's guidance (signaling interest, conversation, managing anxiety) in real dating contexts as practice.

exercise_name: Three-part 'How to Start a Conversation' process
description: Learner follows a simple flexible 3-step opener: just say something (an obvious observation like weather or what they're wearing), then use the reply to keep moving — practiced as an approachable starter drill.
Learner practices 'rooting': using something in the shared environment or context as a natural bridge to ease from an opener into a real conversation.

Learner practices spotting 'free information' (offers/hooks/threads) people reveal and using it to keep conversation going by asking a question or commenting on it — core conversation-threading drill.
Lesson/exercise on generating things to talk about so the learner never runs dry, part of the 3-part starting-a-conversation series.
